Thank you so much, bhai, for such an honest and heartfelt review. ❤️🙏

Lots of love and immense respect from Uttarakhand! ❤️🏔️

Pyre is not just a movie; it is a reflection of the painful reality of Uttarakhand that often goes unnoticed. A heartfelt thank you to Vinod Kapri Ji for bringing this untold side of our beautiful Devbhoomi to the world. 🙏

Every character feels so real, every emotion feels genuine, and every scene connects deeply with the lives of people from our mountains.

Beyond the breathtaking beauty of Uttarakhand, there is another reality — migration, abandoned villages, loneliness, ageing parents, and the silent struggles of those who are left behind.

This film is not just entertainment; it is an emotional message to the government, the younger generation, and society as a whole. We need to understand the pain of our people before our beautiful villages become nothing more than memories.

For the world, it may be a movie. But for those of us who belong to Uttarakhand, it is the story of our own homes, our parents, and our roots. 💔

Thank you once again for giving this beautiful film the recognition it deserves.

PULAVAR – More Than a Film, A Voice That Questions Society!

Some films entertain us, while a few make us think. But rare films leave a lasting impact on our conscience.

Pulavar is not just a film; it is a powerful reflection of the inequalities and social injustices that continue to exist in our society.

Director Murugaiya deserves appreciation for his courage in addressing these uncomfortable realities through cinema.

He has wielded the power of storytelling like a whip against social discrimination and injustice.

Iyakkunar Imayam Bharathiraja delivers one of the most remarkable performances of his career, bringing extraordinary life and depth to his character.

His expressions, silence, and body language speak louder than words.

It is truly moving to witness such a legendary filmmaker's brilliance as an actor in what is described as his final film.

Cinema is not merely about entertainment; it is also about questioning society and awakening its conscience.

Some flowers fade with time, but their fragrance remains forever.

Likewise, Pulavar leaves behind a powerful fragrance of thought and social responsibility.

My heartfelt appreciation to Director Murugaiya and the legendary Bharathiraja.

A film that ends on screen, but its questions continue to live in our minds.

— Suresh Sellaiah
